attribution: Source: Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services, Individual Market Medical Landscape public use file. Calculations and interpretation by CostAnswer; not endorsed by CMS.
columnLayout: 0-7: second-lowest-cost Silver premium, cents, at ages child/18/21/27/30/40/50/60
8-29: silver lowest premium by age (8), median premium by age (8), deductible low/median/high, out-of-pocket maximum low/median/high
30-51: bronze lowest premium by age (8), median premium by age (8), deductible low/median/high, out-of-pocket maximum low/median/high
52-73: gold lowest premium by age (8), median premium by age (8), deductible low/median/high, out-of-pocket maximum low/median/high
74-79: 94% actuarial value Silver deductible low/median/high, out-of-pocket maximum low/median/high
80-85: 87% actuarial value Silver deductible low/median/high, out-of-pocket maximum low/median/high
86-91: 73% actuarial value Silver deductible low/median/high, out-of-pocket maximum low/median/high
-1 means the county publishes no such figure; zero is a real amount.
caveats: These are 2026 plan year premiums as filed with CMS, before any premium tax credit. They are not a quote and do not confirm a plan is available to you.
The landscape file covers the 30 states using HealthCare.gov. 21 states and DC run their own exchanges and publish separately, so they carry no county rows here.
The benchmark is the second-lowest-cost Silver premium in the county, ranked separately at each published age. An enrollee’s actual benchmark depends on who is enrolling and can differ.
Premiums are per person and are added across a household, counting at most the three oldest children under 21, as the federal rating rules require.
Cost-sharing-reduction variants show the deductible and out-of-pocket maximum spread across a county’s Silver plans. They are granted by income, not chosen, and the premium is unchanged.
Deductible and out-of-pocket figures are the individual medical amounts. Drug deductibles, family amounts, copays, and provider networks are outside this snapshot.
validationReport: Resolved every column by header name from the Individual_Market_Medical sheet; a renamed column stops the ingest.
Read 97,082 plan rows across 2055 counties, rejecting duplicate plan and county pairs.
Confirmed no county spans more than one rating area, so a per-county premium is unambiguous.
Kept 2055 counties publishing at least two Silver plans, the minimum a second-lowest-cost benchmark requires; 0 were left out rather than given a substitute benchmark.
Confirmed 2026 counties reproduce the federal default age curve within 0.5% at every published adult age; 29 file their own and are flagged for published-age quoting only.
Verified the benchmark never falls below the lowest Silver premium and that no cost-sharing variant raises the out-of-pocket maximum above standard Silver.
Packed every figure as integer cents and proved the packing lossless by unpacking each county back to its source values.
Stored premiums in USD per month exactly as filed; no inflation, rating, or eligibility adjustment is applied.
